items.titleZh: F1与苹果电视合作成效引关注
items.summaryZh: F1今年在美国转向苹果电视独家转播，F1与苹果称收视与互动表现良好，但第三方机构称家庭触达下降，双方衡量指标不同。
items.originalTitle: Why F1 is so sure its Apple TV deal is working
items.summaryEn: F1 shifted to Apple TV as its exclusive US broadcaster this year, with F1 and Apple citing strong viewership and engagement, while third-party data claims household reach has declined, reflecting differing metrics.
detailZh: F1在美国转向苹果电视，是近年来F1转播格局最大的变化之一——但这笔合作是否见效？
苹果今年成为F1在美国的独家转播方，协议为期五年，标志着F1在可称其最大市场上从线性电视向流媒体服务的重大转变。
F1在今年早些时候的赛季中期报告中表示，苹果带来了“出色的收视与互动表现”；苹果副总裁埃迪·库伊则称，与上一赛季在ESPN相比，收视“在比赛日实现显著的两位数百分比增长，更重要的是在周六”。
但电视分析机构Samba等第三方称，转向苹果电视后家庭触达下降，不过该指标不含观看时长；F1首席执行官斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利称，按观看时长计算，F1今年8月在美国同比增长13%。
F1所有者自由媒体集团的首席执行官兼总裁德里克·张在奥斯汀由The Race和Axios联合举办的“Formula One's Premium Playbook”活动上，与Axios媒体记者萨拉·费舍尔谈到了这一话题。
“去年正是在奥斯汀这里，我们宣布了与苹果的合作协议。当时我们说，‘看，我们所关注的是超越传统转播覆盖范围的东西，也就是我们多年来衡量收视率的方式，或者坦率地说，是参与度，这才是现在真正的关键指标，’”张解释道。
“一年前我们说的是，我们要找的是一个像苹果这样的合作伙伴，其用户群体非常相似，有很好的重叠，然后是苹果生态系统以及我们能利用它做的事情，无论是在Apple News、Apple TV、Apple Store上，还是在你的iPhone上推广比赛。我认为苹果在美国拥有60%的市场份额。
“然后是他们可以在产品上做的许多其他创新内容，我认为他们的工程师一直在努力推进，无论是能够关注你想要的任何车手、拥有多个信号源，还是诸如此类在未来几年只会不断改进的东西。所有这些，在我看来，都完全按计划在推进。
"更重要的是，美国乃至坦率地说全世界的媒体分发格局多年来一直在僵化。现在我们有了一个合作伙伴，它既是分发平台，也是广播机构。
"所以苹果所做的，比如……与Netflix合作，让Netflix能够转播加拿大大奖赛[在美国]，或者苹果拥有《极速求生》第八季，与IMAX影院达成协议，让人们能在影院观看我们的比赛。
"他们能够做到传统广播机构和分发平台做不到的事情，因为后者被合同束缚得太紧、受合同限制太多。
"这是一个不断演变的事情，我们将继续关注。"
Chang 重申了 F1 对 Apple 的承诺，远不止履行这份五年协议。
“我们预期会有一个很棒的合作伙伴。他们的表现完全符合我们的预期，坦率地说甚至更好，”Chang 说道。
“这是众所周知的事。这是一份五年协议，我们完全有意在这段时间内与他们建立出色的合作关系，并希望能延续到之后。”
对 F1 来说，确切的收视人数只是它追求的指标之一。更重要的是它能触达多广泛的受众，即使这意味着车迷以不同的方式参与其中。
“你不再需要把F1当成必须每场比赛都去现场、或者每场比赛都在电视上看才能算粉丝的东西了，对吧？”张说。
“现在，我们当然希望每一位与F1相关的人都能一天24小时关注F1、去每一场比赛或者每场比赛都在电视上看，但我们知道那不会发生，对吧？
“但一项重要的数据是，我们在外面有数亿粉丝，其中60%的粉丝每天都与F1互动。
“显然我们不是每天都比赛。所以这些内容就是……无论是精彩集锦，还是即将到来的比赛的预览，还是生活方式类的东西，对吧？
“像这类人们希望每天参与的内容，能让他们融入这项运动，让他们觉得自己是这项运动的一部分，并且让这项运动始终在他们心中占据首要位置。”
detailEn: Formula 1’s pivot to Apple TV in the United States has been one of the biggest shifts in F1’s broadcast landscape in recent times - but is it paying off?
Apple became the exclusive F1 broadcaster in the US this year with a five-year deal, marking a major shift from linear TV to a streaming service in arguably F1’s biggest market.

F1 said Apple was delivering "excellent viewership and engagement" in its mid-season report earlier this year, while Apple vice president Eddy Cue claimed viewership was "up by significant double-digit percentage growth on the race day, and more importantly on Saturdays" versus the previous season on ESPN.

But third parties such as TV analytics firm Samba have claimed household reach since the switch to Apple TV is down, though that doesn’t include hours watched, a metric by which F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali said F1 was up in the US 13% year-on-year in August.

It’s a topic that CEO and president of F1 owner Liberty Media Derek Chang spoke about with Axios Media Correspondent Sara Fischer at 'Formula One's Premium Playbook', an event hosted by The Race and Axios in Austin.

"It was last year here in Austin that we announced the Apple deal. At the time we said, 'look, what we're looking at is something that goes beyond sort of traditional broadcast reach, which is the way we've measured viewership for however many years, or frankly, engagement, which is really the key metric now'," Chang explained.

"What we said a year ago was, what we're looking for is a partner like Apple [that] has a very similar demographic, great overlap there, and then the Apple ecosystem and what we can do with that, whether it's promoting the races on Apple News, Apple TV, in the Apple Store, on your iPhone. I think Apple has a 60% market share in the US.

"Then a lot of the other innovative stuff they can do with the product, which I think their engineers continue to be hard at work on, whether it's being able to follow whatever driver you want, having multiple feeds, all that sort of stuff that will only improve over the next few years. All of that, to me, has been playing out exactly as planned.

"On top of that, the media distribution landscape in the US, and frankly around the world, has been calcifying for years. Now we've got a partner here who is the distribution platform, as well as the broadcaster.

"So what Apple has done in terms of... doing something with Netflix, where Netflix was able to broadcast the Canadian Grand Prix [in the US], or Apple had Season 8 of Drive to Survive, doing a deal with IMAX Theatres, so that people could view our races in theatres.
"They're able to do things that more traditional broadcasters and distribution platforms, because they're so hung up in their contracts and restricted by their contracts, can't do.
"That's an evolving thing that we’ll continue to watch for."
Chang reaffirmed F1’s commitment to Apple that goes well beyond honouring the five-year deal.
"We anticipated having a great partner. They performed exactly the way we thought and frankly even better," Chang said.
"It's common knowledge. It's a five-year deal and we have every intent of having a great partnership with them during that time and hopefully beyond."
For F1, the exact viewership number is only one of the metrics it's chasing. Far more important is how wide an audience it can reach, even if that means fans are engaging in different ways.
"You no longer think about F1 as something that you've got to go to every race or watch every race on television to be a fan, right?" Chang said.
"Now, we would love every person associated with F1 to follow F1 24 hours a day, go to every race or watch every race on TV, but we know that's not going to happen, right?
"But one of the important stats is that we have hundreds of millions of fans out there [and] 60% of those fans engage with F1 on a daily basis.
"Obviously we don't race every day. So this is content that is... whether it's highlights, whether it's previews of upcoming races, whether it's lifestyle things, right?
"Stuff like that that people want to engage with on a daily basis, and that brings them into the sport, makes them feel like they're part of the sport, and it’s front of mind for those people."
keyPointsZh: 苹果今年成为F1美国独家转播方，协议为期五年，从线性电视转向流媒体。
苹果副总裁埃迪·库伊称比赛日收视实现显著两位数百分比增长，周六增幅更重要。
电视分析机构Samba称转向苹果电视后家庭触达下降，但该指标不含观看时长；F1首席执行官斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利称8月美国观看时长同比增长13%。
keyPointsEn: Apple became F1's exclusive US broadcaster this year under a five-year deal, shifting from linear TV to streaming.
Apple vice president Eddy Cue said viewership saw significant double-digit percentage growth on race day, and more importantly on Saturdays.

TV analytics firm Samba said household reach has declined since the switch to Apple TV, though that metric excludes hours watched; F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali said US hours watched were up 13% year-on-year in August.

items.titleZh: 维斯塔潘回应COTA老板：他开我的车五圈后就走不动了
items.summaryZh: 维斯塔潘认为奥斯汀赛道需要彻底挖开重做地基，仅重新铺设路面不足以解决他所说的“不可接受”的颠簸问题。

media.altZh: 维斯塔潘回应COTA老板：他开我的车五圈后就走不动了 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: Max Verstappen reacts to COTA boss: "He can drive my car, after five laps he won't be able to walk"
items.summaryEn: Verstappen believes the Austin circuit needs to be completely dug up and given a better foundation, saying resurfacing alone is not enough to fix the "unacceptable" bumps.
detailZh: 维斯塔潘回应COTA老板：“他可以开我的车，五圈之后他就走不动了。”
维斯塔潘建议奥斯汀的F1赛道需要彻底挖开并打好更好的地基。这位荷兰车手认为，仅仅重新铺设路面不足以解决“不可接受”的颠簸问题。
这是本周末F1围场的主要话题之一：美洲赛道极端的颠簸。车手们在周五晚的车手会议上提出了他们的担忧，会后维斯塔潘留下与FIA和赛道代表进一步交流了一段时间。
由于赛道建在得克萨斯臭名昭著的高塑性黏土上，它遭受严重的胀缩效应。两年前赛道曾全面重铺，今年赛事前又进行了两次处理。9号弯至11号弯之间的路段再次重铺，同时努力清除12号弯至19号弯之间最严重的颠簸。
然而，据车手们表示，这还不够。维斯塔潘在周四就已经将赛道状况描述为“不可接受”和“失控”，并在周六补充说，他在奥斯汀每天都要服用止痛药，就像兰多·诺里斯每节练习都需要服用头痛药一样。
当排位赛后维斯塔潘在围场接受荷兰媒体采访期间颠簸再次出现时，他说：“这里有几个弯道简直真的不可接受。”
这似乎主要指的是1号弯刹车区域下方的巨大颠簸，以及19号弯一个相当危险的颠簸，但当Motorsport.com向维斯塔潘提出这一点时，他解释说还有更多问题区域。
“1号弯和19号弯确实非常糟糕，但4号弯到5号弯之间的整个高速路段也是，那里的颠簸太大了……我当然理解这里的地面是个问题，但那是你应该事先查看的事情。那真的不应该成为借口。”
除了给车手带来相当大的身体负担外，埃塞斯弯（Esses）的颠簸也具有潜在危险。在奥斯汀的各节练习与排位中，已有数位车手在该处几乎失去对赛车的控制，而如果在这一连串高速弯中真的出现问题，后果可能极其严重。
“是的，那些事情在如此高的速度下真的不应该发生，当时赛车就这样触底了，”维斯塔潘说。
维斯塔潘提出影响深远的措施
美洲赛道主席鲍比·爱泼斯坦回应了维斯塔潘最初的评论，表示实际情况在练习中并没有这位荷兰人说的那么糟糕。
“我们对1号弯底部有颠簸感到不满。我们直到本周才知道这件事。如果知道，我们本会修好它。但马克斯提到的其他事情，即赛道周围所有的颠簸，我们已经修复了。赛道状况非常好，”爱泼斯坦告诉ESPN。
他甚至表示，预计维斯塔潘在周五练习赛后就会改变主意。
“马克斯很少说我错了，但他也经常是对的。他通常非常坦率，我很欣赏他这一点。我对他所说的话没有意见，但我认为他可能会在某些方面感到惊讶，那些他以为存在的颠簸已经不存在了。”
然而，当这些评论在荷兰媒体环节被转述给维斯塔潘时，情况恰恰相反。这位四届世界冠军仍然对赛道的状况远不满意，并认为如果爱泼斯坦驾驶小红牛22，他也会说同样的话。
维斯塔潘说：“我邀请他来开我的车。我觉得他开完五圈就得下车，而且会走不动路。”
据维斯塔潘所说，未来几年需要采取影响深远的措施。周四，他已经表示，由于脊椎受损，F1车手不应再被迫接受这样的条件；排位赛之后，这位荷兰人又为未来几年提出了一个具体建议。
“你可以再铺一层新沥青，但一两年后还会出现同样的问题，所以必须往更深层看。
“我认为国际汽联和F1在这方面也应该更严格。我理解这一切要花很多钱，但这真的只是给问题贴块膏药。如果你知道下面的地基在移动，就得把整个东西挖开，打好合适的地基。”
detailEn: Max Verstappen reacts to COTA boss: "He can drive my car, after five laps he won't be able to walk"

Verstappen suggests that the F1 circuit in Austin needs to be completely dug up and given a better foundation. According to the Dutchman, simply resurfacing the track is not enough to tackle the "unacceptable" bumps

It is one of the main talking points in the Formula 1 paddock this weekend: the extreme bumps at the Circuit of the Americas. Drivers raised their concerns during Friday evening's drivers' briefing, after which Verstappen stayed behind for some time to speak further with representatives of the FIA and the circuit.

Because the track was built on Texas' infamous high-plasticity clay, it suffers from a severe shrink-swell effect. Two years ago, it was completely resurfaced, while two further interventions were carried out ahead of this year's event. The section between Turns 9 and 11 was resurfaced again, while efforts were made to remove the worst bumps between Turns 12 and 19.

According to the drivers, however, that is not enough. Verstappen already described the track conditions as "unacceptable" and "out of control" on Thursday, adding on Saturday that he is taking painkillers every day in Austin, just as Lando Norris needs headache tablets for every session.
When the bumps came up again after qualifying during Verstappen’s Dutch media round in the paddock, he said: "There are a few corners here that are simply really unacceptable."

That appears to refer primarily to the enormous bump under braking for Turn 1 and a rather dangerous one at Turn 19, but when Motorsport.com put that to Verstappen, he explained that there are more problem areas.

"Turns 1 and 19 are indeed really bad, but also that whole fast section between Turns 4 and 5, there are such big bumps there... Of course I understand that the ground here is a problem, but that's something you should have looked at beforehand. That really shouldn't be an excuse."

Besides placing considerable physical strain on the drivers, the bumps through the Esses are also potentially dangerous. Several drivers have already come close to losing control of their cars at that point during the practice sessions in Austin, and if things actually go wrong through the sequence of high-speed corners, the consequences could be immense.
"Yes, those are things that really shouldn't happen at such high speeds, when the car bottoms out like that", Verstappen said.
Verstappen proposes far-reaching measures
Bobby Epstein, chairman of the Circuit of the Americas, responded to Verstappen's initial comments by suggesting that the situation was not as bad in practice as the Dutchman had made it sound.

"We don't feel good that there's a bump at the bottom of Turn 1. We didn't know about it until this week. We would have fixed it. But the other things Max spoke about, all the bumps around the track, we've fixed them. The track is in really good shape", Epstein told ESPN.
He even expressed the expectation that Verstappen would change his mind after Friday practice.

"Max doesn't say I'm wrong a lot, but he's also right a lot. He's usually very frank, and I appreciate that about him. I had no problem with him saying what he said, but I think he might be surprised in some areas that bumps he thought were here aren't [there] anymore."

However, when those comments were put to Verstappen during the Dutch media session, that proved to be anything but the case. The four-time world champion is still far from impressed with the condition of the circuit and believes Epstein would say the same if he were to drive the RB22.
"I invite him to drive my car", Verstappen said. "I think he'd have to get out after five laps and wouldn't be able to walk anymore."

According to Verstappen, far-reaching measures will be needed in the coming years. On Thursday, he had already said that F1 drivers should no longer have to accept such conditions because of the damage to their spines, and after qualifying the Dutchman put forward a concrete proposal for the years ahead.
"You can put down a new layer of asphalt again, but a year or two later you'll have the same problem, so you need to look deeper.

"I think the FIA and Formula 1 should also be stricter about that. I understand that it all costs a lot of money, but this is really just putting a plaster over the problem. You need to dig the whole thing up and put in a proper foundation if you know the ground underneath is moving."
keyPointsZh: 车手们在周五晚的车手会议上提出了对颠簸的担忧，维斯塔潘会后留下与FIA及赛道代表进一步交流
赛道建在得克萨斯高塑性黏土上，受严重胀缩效应影响；两年前曾全面重铺，今年赛前又进行了两次处理
9号弯至11号弯之间路段再次重铺，12号弯至19号弯之间则努力清除最严重的颠簸
keyPointsEn: Drivers raised concerns about the bumps during Friday evening's drivers' briefing, after which Verstappen stayed behind to speak further with FIA and circuit representatives
The track was built on Texas' high-plasticity clay and suffers from a severe shrink-swell effect; it was completely resurfaced two years ago, with two further interventions ahead of this year's event
The section between Turns 9 and 11 was resurfaced again, while efforts were made to remove the worst bumps between Turns 12 and 19

items.summaryEn:
🗣️: "I started racing when I was eight or nine years old and it was just me and my parents. 
"My dad was my mechanic, and my mum came to every single race I’ve ever done. 
"They’ve made so many sacrifices and really put their lives on pause to allow me to live my dream. I’m just so glad to repay them."
#F1Academy || #USGP 🇺🇸
detailZh:
🗣️： "我八岁或九岁开始赛车，那时候只有我和我的父母。 
"我爸爸是我的机械师，我妈妈参加了我所参加的每一场比赛。 
"他们做出了很多牺牲，真的把他们的生活暂停下来，让我能够实现我的梦想。我只是非常高兴能够回报他们。"
